title: Replying to @𝐂𝐚𝐬𝐞𝐲 𝐑𝐞𝐞𝐝 Non-spoiler thoughts on the cast and new char...
transcript: Okay, so I did not get a chance to talk about the cast in my original smash video, so let's talk about the cast, because holy shit, it was like an insanely stacked cast. So you had Chris Rodriguez, Brooks Ashmanskis, Robin Herder, Alex Brightman, and then all the way on the right there is event Nicole Brown. I think that Robin is just perfect casting for any character that is going to play Marilyn Monroe. Like, it just works so well. I will say, of all the characters, I really was not a huge fan of the way they handled the Ivy character in the show. But that's not really Robin's fault. That's more of a book problem. For me, the standout was Brooks Ashmanskis as the director character. His name is Nigel in the show, and he is very different from Derek in the TV show, but he is absolutely hilarious. He's given all of the funniest jokes and is really making a meal of this role. Then you have Chris Rodriguez and Alex Brightman. They play the Tom and Julia writer characters of the show. Unlike in the TV show, their characters are married to each other in this, and I thought their dynamic was really great. They both nail the comedy, obviously, but mostly played the straight men to the chaos that is going on around them. I do love that they still gave Crystal Rodriguez's character a scarf though, which is a reference to the Wild scarves that Deborah Messing's character wore on the original show. Just have event. Nicole Brown, who's on the right over there. Now, I know her mostly from Drake and Josh and community, and her character is basically just Helen if she was a Broadway producer. And it was so cool to see her live. I thought she was fantastic. The person not pictured here is John Allen Saxer as Karen. It will say the character of Karen is much smaller in this version than it was on the TV show, where she is basically the co lead of the show. But for this version of Karen, I thought John Allen was perfect for what they were going for, which was like a much nicer, chipier version of the character.
